title: security: rbac-v2 - enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging + residency hardening
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: tighten RBAC v2 enforcement for KMS region pinning and data residency while adding explicit audit logging hooks for all key-related policy decisions. This PR implements the server-side enforcement path (opt-in via feature flag), improves audit event semantics, and adds a migration/backfill job to tag existing secrets with residency metadata.

What changed (high level): - RBAC v2 policy evaluation: new policy predicates `kms_region_allowed` and `residency_policy_evaluator` that are evaluated at decision time. - Enforcement: when feature flag `rbac_v2_kms_enforce` is enabled, requests that violate KMS region pinning are rejected with structured error codes and audit entries. - Audit logging: introduced new audit event types `KMS_REGION_PIN_VIOLATION` and `RESIDENCY_ENFORCEMENT_CHECK` with standardized fields (actor, resource, policy, decision, source_region, key_arn). - KMS integration: added adapter layer in keymanager to return region metadata and added validation path in crypto-service. - Migration: background job `tag-residency-metadata` to populate residency tags on existing customer keys and secrets; job is idempotent and throttled. - Tests/docs: new unit and integration tests, updated RBAC v2 docs and a CLI helper for operators to preview policy impact.

Why this is safe: enforcement is behind feature flag and rollout plan in the PR description. Default behavior remains audit-only until a progressive rollout is completed. Error codes are non-breaking and clients receive explicit guidance in the response body when a request is blocked.

Rollout plan: 1) deploy with `rbac_v2_kms_enforce=false` (audit-only) for 48 hours, monitor audit logs and console alerts. 2) roll out migration job to tag existing keys. 3) enable enforcement for 5% of traffic, monitor for false positives. 4) ramp to 100% if no issues.

Related: ENG-2148, SEC-3091. See inline commits for smaller change sets.
